beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: In the heat of the day, three travelers appeared at Abraham's tent. He did not know at first who they were. He only knew they were strangers, and tired, and that hospitality was sacred.

timing.text: In the heat of the day, three travelers appeared at Abraham's tent.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He washed their feet, baked fresh bread, set out the best he had, and waited on them himself under the oak. And as they ate, they brought him astonishing news — and a heavy word about Sodom.

timing.text: He washed their feet, baked fresh bread, set out the best he had, and waited on them himself under the oak.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: For those cities had grown very dark, and judgment was near. Two of the travelers went on ahead. But Abraham stayed behind, standing before the warm presence of the Lord — and he began to plead.

timing.text: For those cities had grown very dark, and judgment was near.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Not for himself. For strangers — for the good people who might still be down in that doomed city.

timing.text: Not for himself.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked? Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?

timing.text: Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?
Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes.

timing.text: If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Yes, God said. And you can almost feel Abraham's courage grow. What about forty-five? What about forty? Thirty? Each time, gently, the answer came back — yes. Yes. I will spare it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He is not wearing God down. He is discovering how merciful God already is — how much God would rather spare than destroy. So Abraham dares one last step.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once: Peradventure ten shall be found there.

timing.text: Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once: Peradventure ten shall be found there.

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: I will not destroy it for ten's sake.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Let me speak just once more, Abraham said. What if there are only ten?

timing.text: Let me speak just once more, Abraham said.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: For the sake of ten good people, the whole place would be spared. That is the God Abraham found at the top of that hill. Not one straining to condemn — one who could be talked, again and again, toward mercy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Abraham went home in the dusk, amazed. He had dared to plead for strangers, and found God kinder than he had hoped. God let a man argue with him — and kept saying yes.

card.text: God let one old man plead for strangers, and answered mercy every time. He is not looking for reasons to condemn — he welcomes the bold and the interceding. What would you dare ask him for?
